newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST - Australian Sports News - July 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Australian Sports News - July 25.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Australian cyclist Neil Stephens, who competes for the Spanish Festina team, yesterday achieved the greatest moment of his sporting career by winning the 17th stage of the Tour de France. Stephens, from Canberra, became the first Australian since Phil Anderson in 1991 to win a stage of the Tour. Page 24.

Russian swimmer Alex Popov, the number one swimmer in the world, will represent Russia at the European Championships in August, but has been well embraced here in Australia. Popov, who trains at the Australian Institute of Sport eight months of the year, yesterday put his support behind 14-year-old Ian Thorpe, who will become the youngest man to represent Australia at the Pan Pacifics in Japan next month. Page 22.

While Australian basketballer Michelle Timms has a high profile in the United States Women's National Basketball Association, her salary is about half that of Australian team member Shelley Sandie, who plays for the San Jose Lasers in the rival American Bsketball League. Page 23.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

The fourth Ashes cricket Test at Headingly between Australia and England was delayed by rain after Australian captain Mark Taylor won the toss and sent England in to bat. Earlier, Australian manager Alan Crompton formally objected to the position taken b England's chairman of selectors David Graveney in relations to the switch in pitches. Page 44.

Australian rugby union captain John Eales said yesterday his team would not be intimidated by the New Zealand All Blacks in the Bledisloe Cup match to be played in Melbourne tomorrow. The All Blacks are favoured to win, givent they have won seven of their last eight outings against the Wallabies. Page 44.

The International Amateur Athletic Federation says athletes are free to carry whatever flag they wish at the world track and field championships in Athens next week, which could lead to a flurry of Aboriginal flags on display should elite Australian nativ sprinters Cathy Freeman, Nova Peris-Kneebone, Kyle Vander-Kuyp or Patrick Johnson win any medals. Page 44.
THE AGE

Simon Minton-Connell has been dropped from the Western Bulldogs Australian Football League team, despite his impressive first half performance to the season which places him fifth on the AFL goal-kicking table. However, the full-forward has lost his confidence, and has only kicked three goals in the last three games. Page D2.

Australian Football League clubs are expected to attack the governing body if it attempts to invest any of the A$40 million television rights sweetener it expects from the Docklands Stadium. Most club presidents said yesterday they backed the Docklands project in March on the basis that the AFL would only invest A$30 million - money to be generated from the sale of Waverley. Page D3.

The Australian world gymnastics championship trials will be held in Melbourne tonight at the Glasshouse. The trials are expected to showcase the new wave of Australia's young gymnastic talent, as many of the older gymnasts chose to end their careers afte the Atlanta Olympics last year. Page D11.
THE HERALD SUN

Australian tennis player Mark Philippoussis yesterday fought back from being a set and a break down to move into the quarter finals of the A$410,000 Los Angeles men's tournament. Philippoussis, who is ranked third in the tournament, defeated fellow Austrlian Sandon Stolle 3-6, 6-4, 6-3. Page 89.

The 2,380 metres Australian Oaks harness race at Moonee Valley on Saturday night will be a clash between the three "supermodels" of the sport, Kates First, Concorde Lombo, and Sheza Mona. The race will decide which horse is Australia's best three-year-old filly. Page 93.

Neil King, the former chief executive of Athletics Australia and new chief executive of the Geelong Australian Football League club, yesterday deflected questions about troubled Geelong player Gary Ablett, comparing his struggles with the troubled retirement of marathon runner Lisa Ondieki. Page 94.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Australian golfer Ian Baker-Finch said his 92 in the British Open in Scotland annoyed him so much he quit the tournament, but just as annoying is the Australian media's fascination with his continued failure to rejuvenate his fame. Yesterday he competed in the more relaxed Queensland PGA event at The Willows. Page 126.

New Zealand rugby union coach John Hart is fuming at reports his team snubbed Victorian Premier Jeff Kennett at a reception yesterday. Hart said that the run-on players for the Bledisloe Cup match against Australia tomorrow night rested in their hotel intead of attending, and said this was an arrangement made two months ago. Page 124.

Sydney will not host the final of the Commonwealth Bank Netball Trophy even if its two teams, the Swifts and the Sandpipers, make it through to the decider. Tournament organisers were forced to book events well in advance to secure venues, a process that had to take place before the make up of the final four is decided. The finals will beheld on Adelaide with the grand finals held in Melbourne. Page 123.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
